23. ISSUE No.2 in MVC No.5476/2021:-
This petition is filed for seeking compensation of Rs.30,00,000/- for the injuries sustained by the petitioner in the road traffic accident.
As stated above, the petitioner has already proved that, the accident was occurred due to sole negligence on the part of rider of offending Motor cycle.
The petitioner contended that, he has sustained grievous injuries in the alleged accident.

He further stated that, he has taken treatment at SNR hospital, Kolar as an inpatient and spent  14 MVC.5476/2021 c/w 5477/2021  SCCH-10 more than Rs.5,00,000/- towards medical and incidental expenses and supposed to spent more amount in future.

24. Before proceeding to discuss this issue, I feel it necessary to reproduce the law declared by the Hon'ble Apex Court in a decision reported in 2011(1) S.C.C page 343 in the case of Rajkumar Vs. Ajay Kumar.
In para No.5 of the judgment, Hon'ble Apex Court has mentioned the heads under which compensation is to be awarded in personal injury cases.
I reproduce the same hereunder for convenience.

awarded in personal injury cases are the following;
 Pecuniary damages (special damages)

(i) Expenses relating to treatment,
 hospitalization, Medicines, transportation,
 nourishing food and miscellaneous expenditure.

Loss of earnings (and other gains) which the  injured would have made had he not been  injured, comprising):
 a. Loss of earning during the period of  treatment;
 15 MVC.5476/2021 c/w 5477/2021  SCCH-10  b. Loss of future earning on account of  permanent disability.
 Future Medical expenses.
 Non-pecuniary damages (general damages)
 Damages for pain, suffering and trauma as a  consequence of the injuries.
 Loss of amenities (and / or loss of prospects of  marriage)
 Loss of expectation of life (shortening of normal  longevity).
25.

33. On perusal of the medical documents and medical evidence it is crystal clear that, the petitioner cannot do his normal work as he was doing earlier.
Hence, the disability of the petitioner will definitely come in the way of the petitioner in his future earnings.
As per the doctor, the whole body disability is 23%.
It is settled principles
that all permanent disabilities arising out of injuries do not result in loss of earning capacity.
The percentage of loss of earning capacity is not the same as the percentage of permanent disability.

Even though the doctor has opined 23%
permanent disability to the whole body, considering the nature of work of the petitioner and considering the disability, I assess the petitioner's loss of future earning capacity as 15%.

The loss of future earning capacity is assessed as 15%.
The annual income is assessed Rs.1,80,000/-(Rs.15,000 x 12).

Therefore,
the loss of future income would be Rs.1,80,000/- (annual income) X 15 (multiplier) X 15% = Rs.4,05,000/-.

Hence, the Parvatamma vs Rajesh.A on 10 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/101811139/

sentences.text: 49. It has been held by Hon'ble Apex Court as well as Hon'ble High Court that, even in the case of breach of policy conditions, the compensation determined must be first paid by the insurer, who could thereafter recover the same from the owner of the offending vehicle.

50. In the present case on hand, though there is violation of policy condition by the owner of the insured vehicle, since the petitioners being third parties, at the first instance the insurer i.e. respondent No.2 has to pay the award amount of Rs.4,83,500/- to the petitioner in MVC No.5476/2021 and Rs.25,000/- to the petitioner in MVC No.5477/2021 with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of petition till the date of deposit, then same has to be recovered from the owner  28 MVC.5476/2021 c/w 5477/2021  SCCH-10 (respondent No.1) of the offending vehicle in accordance with law.
